statement: The nonnegative walking-complex category is not Frobenius over a nonzero ring; stalk R[0] is projective but not injective.
notes: Refutes the Frobenius identification in Lead L3; finite F_2 certificate.

statement: For every commutative ring, relative left-exact functors out of bounded nonnegative finite-free complexes are fully faithfully determined by their disk values; the essential image is the explicit finite-matrix kernel condition.
notes: Ordinary categorical kernels; no regularity, field, or domain assumption.

statement: Over a PID the essential image is characterized by cycle kernels and two-term torsion-block kernels; cycle kernels alone are insufficient for nonfields.
notes: Z/4 target counterexample; distinguishes PID from principal ideal rings with zero divisors.

statement: For every commutative ring and Quillen exact target, exact functors correspond to admissible resolutions; strong relative-left-exactness has the stated additional admissible-kernel criterion.
notes: Quillen axioms hold in the theorem, not in the incomplete printed Sex1-2 list; shorter strong criterion requires weak idempotent completeness.

statement: The printed Sex1-2 axioms alone do not imply the essential-image characterization by resolutions.
notes: Finite counterexample in finite abelian groups, using pullback of Z/16 to Z/4 along multiplication by2.

statement: The category of bounded finite-free complexes in all integer degrees is Frobenius; its stable category is K^b(free).
notes: Corrected two-sided Frobenius statement; does not identify this enlargement with the manuscript nonnegative category.

statement: Dold-Puppe decomposition L_n=direct_sum_i N_i(L)^(binomial(n,i)); termwise finite/projective equivalences.
notes: Equation3.3, Theorem3.6, Corollary3.8 opened; count of surjections derived.

statement: For any commutative ring and finite simplicial terms, normalization is bounded in degreeD iff all residue-field rank functions are eventually polynomial of uniformly bounded degreeD.
notes: Maximal ideals suffice; eventual equality upgrades to equality at every nonnegative n.

statement: Over every regular noetherian ring, partial-perfection is equivalent to finite bounded homology; the uniform raw-rank criterion implies perfection but characterizes actual boundedness.
notes: No finite Krull dimension assumption; cited theorem opened and hypotheses translated.

statement: Proposition1(e) is false in both directions even over Z; uniform degrees fix sufficiency but not necessity for derived perfection.
notes: Distinct-prime unbounded homology and locally finite contractible disk complex.

statement: Over a noetherian ring, pseudo-coherent normalization is perfect exactly when derived residue-field homology has a uniform bound; bounded raw normalization need not be perfect on a nonregular ring.
notes: Complete finite characteristic-two dual-number counterexample and all-degree periodic Tor calculation.

statement: Under noetherianness the binomial fiber coefficients are constructible; PID rank N_i includes mu_i+mu_i+1+beta_i+beta_i+1+nu_i; derived perfection permits infinitely many contractible disk factors.
notes: Both terms mu_i and mu_i+1 are necessary; strict versus derived finite-support criteria distinguished; disk certificate included.
